# Dock Layouts becomes a guide series: adopt, mechanics, features, UI

## Context

`learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayouts.md` (`#17514`, merged 2026-08-21) is the subsystem's first architecture guide — an intro: the ownership loop, one gesture end to end, the four-row state discipline, the adoption checklist, the wire vocabulary, the traps. It reviewed at 9/10, and it is one page for a subsystem of 29 engine modules, four host apps, and a multi-window choreography.

Operator direction (2026-08-22): once the host-class debt is resolved, double down on guides — mechanics, features, and how docking connects to ordinary Neo UIs — as a series, with one mental model at the front: *a human or an AI peer asking "how can I use and configure it inside MY Neo app?"*

## The Problem

The intro answers "what is this and why does it work"; it does not answer the adopter's questions in order. Today a reader who wants docking in their own app has to reverse-engineer one of the hosts (4–5k lines each until the host class lands), the ADR, and the model contract. The Knowledge Base inherits the same gap: a question about configuring panes, vessels, perspectives or auto-hide in a consumer app has no single guide to cite, so answers are stitched from the ADR and source.

**Why an epic:** each guide is its own authored, reviewed, tree-registered artifact under `guide-authoring` (grounding, render-verified Mermaid, cross-family review); the set shares one mental model, one vocabulary, and one sequencing constraint (the adoption guide must teach `extends DockWorkspace`, so it lands after the host class) — coordination a single ticket cannot carry.

## Intended Solution Shape

A series under the existing `guides/uibuildingblocks` tree node, the intro kept as its front door and each part answering one adopter question in the order an adopter asks it: adopting and configuring docking in your own app (document, panes, policies, vessel render target, persistence, theming by tokens); the mechanics as they run (gesture, claim, vessel lifecycle, conversion, reintegration); the features (perspectives, auto-hide rails, grouped drag, overflow, keyboard); and how it connects to Neo UIs (panes as ordinary components — state providers, stores, tab containers, controllers, layouts). Every part follows the house pattern the intro established (ownership loop plus one-gesture pairing, claims with receipts, traps with tickets), and every code example runs against the engine class, not a hand-rolled host. Placement inside the tree, part naming and the exact split are the first leaf's structural pre-flight, not this body's.

## Out of Scope

- Rewriting the intro (`DockLayouts.md`) beyond the one correction the host-class epic owes it.
- Reference documentation generated from JSDoc; the ADR and the model contract stay the authority tiers.
- Video or film assets (the `#15252` arc).

## Avoided Traps

- **One giant page.** The intro is already at the length where a reader stops; the series exists so each part can go deep.
- **Teaching the hand-rolled host.** A guide written against today's 5k-line hosts teaches the debt; the adoption part sequences after the engine class.
- **Prose over receipts.** The house pattern cites a witness for every mechanical claim; a guide part without receipts fails its own review.

## Decision Record impact

none — the guides describe; ADR 0029 and `DockZoneModel.md` decide.

## Sequencing update 2026-08-28 — parts 2–4 wait for the v13.2 greenfield rewrite (D#17818)

The operator-ruled hard-cut rewrite (Discussion #17818) renames the package anatomy, class namespace, and wire vocabulary this series teaches. Disposition, recorded by the epic owner:

- **Part 1 (the adoption guide): SHIPPED** — and it is explicitly inside the rewrite's own guide-update scope, so the rewrite carries its refresh.
- **Parts 2–4 (mechanics, features, panes) are sequenced BEHIND the rewrite.** Authoring them now would teach class names and schema strings the cut renames — the exact rot class this series' own lint rule exists to prevent.
- **At the rewrite's implementation-epic filing, parts 2–4 fold there as guide leaves** (the rewrite's expected target is code-and-guide leaves only), and this epic closes as superseded by that epic.

No part-2/3/4 sub files under this epic before the cut lands.

## Structural pre-flight (leaf 1, #17569 — recorded before authoring)

**Placement: flat siblings under `guides/uibuildingblocks`, prefix-grouped.** The node's own precedent decides it: `HtmlTemplates` + `HtmlTemplatesUnderTheHood` are related flat leaves grouped by name prefix; no nested folder exists anywhere in the node, and inventing one for this series would be a navigation novelty the tree does not need. The intro stays `guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayouts` as the front door.

**The split, ratified as sketched — four parts, one adopter question each, in the order an adopter asks:**

| Part | id | Name | The one question |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (#17569, this leaf) | `DockLayoutsAdoption` | Dock Layouts: Adopting in Your App | "How do I get this into MY app, and what decisions are mine?" |
| 2 | `DockLayoutsMechanics` | Dock Layouts: The Mechanics | "What actually happens when I drag, tear out, come back?" |
| 3 | `DockLayoutsFeatures` | Dock Layouts: The Feature Set | "What does the landed feature surface offer and how do I switch it on?" |
| 4 | `DockLayoutsPanes` | Dock Layouts: Panes Are Ordinary Components | "How does docking meet the rest of my Neo UI — providers, stores, controllers?" |

**SEO:** each part enters the `PRIORITIES` map in `buildScripts/docs/seo/generate.mjs` at `0.8`, the intro's weight. Generated outputs (`sitemap.xml`, `llms.txt`) stay untouched per the pipeline-ownership rule.

**Sequencing:** part 1 lands first and fixes the series vocabulary (the five adopter decisions); parts 2–4 open for self-select once it merges — each is a self-contained leaf under `guide-authoring` with its own cross-family review.

Grounding note for part 1's review: the class and both live consumers were built/migrated by this author this week (#17541 / #17546), and the memory-mine surfaced the lineage the guide stands on — the operator-directed standalone example (#13247), the Qt-ADS differentiator analysis (worker-owned JSON model + multi-window object permanence), and the two-home placement ruling. Every snippet will be consistency-checked against `examples/dashboard/dock/` and `apps/workstation/` at head.

⚠️

- open #17574 — cross-cutting guide-lint guard.

Incremental sub creation is correct, so this does **not** block #17574; however, #17540 is not closeable until those three content outcomes have owning leaves and delivered artifacts. #17574 is coherent under this parent because it protects every remaining part from tracker-id decay—it is enabling substrate, not a substitute for a missing guide.

Stage 3.1 evidence matrix: N/A. These are documentation/lint surfaces fully coverable by source consistency, guide rendering, lint, and cross-family review; no operator-gated runtime effect is a parent success criterion.

### Stage 4 — Prescription Layer

⚠️ with a measured refinement

- #17569 was prescribed at the correct layer and is merged.
- #17574 belongs in the existing `ai/scripts/lint/lint-guides.mjs` + its unit contract; no sibling lint script is needed.
- **Measured constraint:** running the current full lint rule-set over all 56 files under `learn/guides/**` yields **1 unrelated HARD** (the dead link in `fundamentals/ApplicationBootstrap.md`) plus **50 warnings**. Therefore the implementation should use the ticket comment's target-scoped branch: recursively discover `learn/guides/**/*.md` for the no-ticket-id rule while preserving the current general-rule surface for `learn/agentos/*.md` and `learn/benefits/*.md`. Widening every existing rule would couple legacy guide debt into this leaf and make the new guard unmergeable for the wrong reason.

The red control must enter through the real CLI/discovery path, so “a file was passed directly to a pure helper” cannot satisfy the added coverage claim.

### Stage 5 — Avoided Traps Completeness

⚠️

The epic already rejects the giant-page, hand-rolled-host, and prose-without-receipts paths. Two additions are worth retaining for the remaining series:

1. **A guard that never traverses the series tree is decorative.** #17574 must prove a real `learn/guides` file is discovered and can fail.
2. **Do not widen unrelated legacy lint debt into the guide series.** The measured 1-hard/50-warning corpus is the reason for path-scoped rule application.

The no-ticket-id rule should include prose, inline code, and fenced examples unless an independently valid timeless-code counterexample is found and documented; code-fence exemption would reopen the easiest paste-around.
